summary: A dense worker-placement/dice-drafting euro where the die you take doubles as a resource and dictates your next action, forcing constant lookahead planning across five interlocking districts. It plays like a tighter, more tactical cousin of Tascini's other dice-driven designs, with area-majority scoring for building placement layered on top of engine-building.
praised: The die-as-resource-and-action-selector mechanism feels genuinely novel and creates satisfying forward-planning puzzles
Strong production values and thematic board depicting the districts of Ur
Multiple viable paths to points (construction, temple favor, ships) give replayability
Rewards efficient turn optimization for players who like tight euro puzzles
criticised: Steep rules overhead and iconography that make the first few plays confusing
Long playtime (2 hours) that can drag, especially at 4 players with downtime between turns
Some randomness in which dice/values are available can undercut careful planning
Considered one of Tascini's more inaccessible designs, overwhelming for less experienced euro gamers

interaction.kind: area majority and competition for districts/dice, indirect blocking

scoring.why: Points come from building construction and area majority, temple/king's favor tracks, ship abilities, and end-game bonuses, so winners typically balance several of these rather than maxing one.
